findings.explanation: description contradicts spl: the SPL alerts when limits are ABSENT (mem_limit_flag=0 / cpu_hard_cap_flag=0), when declared and cgroup-enforced limits drift more than 3%, or when limits break container_limit_policy.csv bands; it does not page when limits are > 0, does not group by `]`, and uses no `exemptions` lookup. A reader would build the inverse detection.
findings.quote: Rolls up `unlimited_window_sum` by `host_id`, `container_id`, `]`, `environment` across `the scheduled window` and pages when `memory_bytes_declared` > 0, `nano_cpus_declared` > 0, `cpu_quota` > 0, or `nano_cpus_declared` > 0. Uses lookup `exemptions.",`
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite: 'Compares each running container's docker inspect HostConfig limits (Memory, NanoCpus, CpuQuota/CpuPeriod) with the cgroup v2 memory.max/cpu.max actually enforced and with per-image/environment bands in container_limit_policy.csv; returns one row per host_id+container_id when production containers have no memory limit or no hard CPU cap, when declared and enforced limits differ by more than 3%, or when limits fall outside the policy floor/ceiling.'

findings.explanation: Splunk_TA_nix ships no linux:cgroup:limits sourcetype or cgroup-reading script; its documented sourcetypes are cpu, vmstat, df, ps, top, interfaces, etc. The cgroup collector is a customer-written scripted input that can merely be packaged alongside the TA.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux ([Splunkbase 833](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/833)) for linux:cgroup:limits scripted inputs reading cgroup v2 memory.max and cpu.max
findings.suggested_fix: State that linux:cgroup:limits comes from a custom scripted input (optionally deployed in a local app next to Splunk_TA_nix), not from the add-on itself; list the script's expected output fields.

findings.explanation: dataSources and implementation name 'Splunk Add-on for Linux' while app names 'Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (833)'. These are different products: Splunk Add-on for Linux is Splunkbase 3412 (Splunk_TA_linux, collectd metrics over HEC/TCP), which also does not read cgroup files.
findings.quote: sourcetype=linux:cgroup:limits from Splunk Add-on for Linux scripted reads of leaf-scope memory.max and cpu.max
findings.suggested_fix: Use one consistent collector description in dataSources, implementation and detailedImplementation: a custom cgroup scripted input (optionally co-deployed with Splunk_TA_nix 833).

findings.explanation: The SPL reads raw docker:inspect and linux:cgroup:limits events and uses no data model; neither sourcetype is normally CIM-tagged for Change or Inventory, so the listed models do not describe this detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the CIM models (raw-sourcetype detection) or document the eventtype/tag mapping that would make docker:inspect populate Inventory, and only then keep it.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are template text (maintenance windows shifting unlimited_window_sum, batch 'sum', synthetic probes) that do not describe how this SPL actually produces false rows.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `host_id`, `container_id`, `]`, `environment` — Health checks in `oti_containers` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: inspect events missing HostConfig_* aliases (the SPL defaults them to 0, so the container looks unlimited); containers with no environment label landing in 'unknown'; short-lived CI/build containers; cgroup v1 or cgroupfs-driver hosts where memory.max/cpu.max paths do not exist; Docker rounding memory to page size causing small drift; image_key mismatches between digest and tag in the policy CSV.

findings.explanation: The closing checklist, 'severity maps to the six mandated tier strings' and 'twelve mandated fields' are authoring-spec residue addressed to the generator, not implementation guidance for the reader.
findings.quote: Closing checklist: monitoringType lists Configuration and Compliance; splunkPillar Observability; cimModels lists Change and Inventory; equipment lists docker and linux; equipmentModels lists docker_engine and linux_cgroup_v2; five step headers use plain em dashes;
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the closing checklist and the 'mandated' references; keep only operational steps.

findings.explanation: For join, max=0 means unlimited matches per row; it permits fan-out rather than preventing it (default max=1).
findings.quote: uses type=left max=0 to avoid lookup explosions
findings.suggested_fix: Say max=0 keeps all matching subsearch rows, and rely on the preceding stats ... BY host_id, container_id to guarantee one row per key.

findings.explanation: Docker documents --memory-swap=-1 as unlimited swap without version hedging, and an unset --memory-swap with --memory set allows swap equal to the memory limit; the earlier claim that 'negative MemorySwap values mean Docker defaults' is also wrong.
findings.quote: MemorySwap at -1 can mean unlimited swap allowance depending on daemon version
findings.suggested_fix: State: MemorySwap=-1 is unlimited swap; MemorySwap equal to Memory disables swap; unset with Memory set allows swap equal to Memory.

findings.explanation: After stats there is one row per container, sorted by container_id, so unlimited_window_sum counts unlimited containers among up to 10 neighbouring container IDs on a host; it is not a time trend, yet description and visualization present it as the core metric.
findings.quote: streamstats window=10 sums fleet_unlimited_mem along recent ordered samples per host_id as a coarse unlimited-container trend context column
findings.suggested_fix: Describe it as 'unlimited containers among the last 10 rows for this host (ordering is by container_id)', or replace it with eventstats count(eval(mem_limit_flag=0)) BY host_id.

findings.explanation: Unnamed 'postmortems' and Kubernetes VPA guidance are not evidence for a Docker-host control; detailedImplementation also claims the weekly CSV 'satisfies' PCI DSS, SOC 2 CC6.6 and ISO 27001 A.12.1.3, which a configuration report alone cannot prove. status 'verified' has no named SME reviewer.
findings.quote: External references include Docker default unlimited memory case studies in production postmortems, Kubernetes Vertical Pod Autoscaler guidance
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the saved-search/lookup/export evidence, drop unnamed case studies and VPA, change 'satisfy' to 'supports', and set status to draft until an SME signs off.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Missing HostConfig fields are coalesced to the string "0" (memory, NanoCpus, CpuQuota), so an inspect event from an exporter that uses different field names is classified as unlimited and raises critical_unlimited_memory_in_production. Default to null and treat missing values as 'unknown' instead.

Every coalesce line wraps values in camelCase toString(); the Search Reference documents only lowercase tostring() and states eval expressions are case-sensitive. Confirm on a Splunk instance that toString() is accepted; if not, the search errors at parse time.

A non-production container with a memory limit but no hard CPU cap gets severity low_baseline_drift but policy_compliance falls through to compliant_or_review, so the final where drops it; the severity branch is dead for that case.
tstats count FROM Change BY All_Changes.object All_Changes.action has no relation to container resource limits, cgroup drift or policy bands and would not reproduce any row of the primary search.

summary: The SPL and detailedImplementation describe a real governance detector (missing limits, policy ceilings/floors, inspect-vs-cgroup drift), but the description is garbled template text with inverted alert logic, the app field credits the Unix and Linux add-on with a cgroup sourcetype it does not ship, and CIM/KFP/evidence text is generic.
